facts.statement: Pessopteryx fossils date to the Early Triassic period.
The genus Pessopteryx was named by Carl Wiman in 1910.
Historical names for this genus include Merriamosaurus hulkei, Omphalosaurus niesseri, and Rotundopteryx hulkei.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Merriamosaurus hulkei Maisch & Matzke, 2002 Omphalosaurus niesseri (Wiman, 1910) Rotundopteryx hulkei Maisch & Matzke, 2000 non Duckhouse, 1999

facts.statement: Pessopteryx was an extinct ichthyosaur that lived in Svalbard, Norway, during the Early Triassic (Olenekian).
facts.quote: Pessopteryx is an extinct genus of ichthyosaur from the Early Triassic (Olenekian) of Svalbard, Norway.

facts.statement: Carl Wiman originally described four species in the genus Pessopteryx in 1910.
facts.quote: The genus originally contained four species, P. nisseri, P. arctica, P. pinguis, and P. minor, which were named in 1910 by Carl Wiman.

facts.statement: Currently, only P. nisseri is considered a valid species, while others are either nomina dubia or reassigned to other genera.
facts.quote: Only P. nisseri is still considered valid; P. arctica and P. pinguis are considered nomina dubia while P. minor was reassigned to the tenuous genus Isfjordosaurus.

facts.statement: Sander et al. (2026) debated the classification of this species, suggesting it belongs to the genus Omphalosaurus.
facts.quote: In their 2026 publication on omphalosaurid diversity, Sander et al. considered this species to belong to the genus Omphalosaurus (O. nisseri).

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the available fossil data for Pessopteryx is non-diagnostic due to its limited nature.
facts.quote: They regarded the hypodigm as non-diagnostic based on the limited available data.

facts.statement: Pessopteryx belongs to the parent group Merriamosauridae.
Pessopteryx is classified within the family Merriamosauridae.
Pessopteryx is classified as a reptile.
